{"status": "NO_PLAN", "reasons": ["CS4246 requires CS3263, which requires CS2109S, CS2040C/S, MA1522/MA1513/MA1508E/MA2001, and EE2012/ST2131/MA2116/ST2334/MA2216. CS2109S requires CS2040C/S and MA1511+1512 or MA1521. CS2040C/S requires CS1010. CS1231 is not a prerequisite for any of these, so it is not needed. However, ST2334 and EE2012 are mutually exclusive with other required stats/math courses or each other in a way that creates a conflict? No, ST2334 and EE2012 are not mutually exclusive. But ST2334 requires MA1505/1511/1512/1521/2002. EE2012 requires MA1511+1512. MA1522 has no prereqs. The conflict is that CS3263 requires (MA2001 or MA1522 or MA1513 or MA1508E or MA1101R) AND (EE2012A or EE2012 or ST2131 or MA2116 or MA2116T or ST2334 or MA2216). We can pick MA1522 and EE2012. But EE2012 requires MA1511+1512. So Sem 1: CS1010, MA1511, MA1512. Sem 2: CS2040C, MA1522, EE2012. Sem 3: CS2109S. Sem 4: CS3263. Sem 5: CS4246. This works. Why did the user say ST2334 and EE2012 exclude each other? They don't. But ST2334 is mutually exclusive with ST2131, MA2116, etc. EE2012 is mutually exclusive with EE2012A, ST2334, ST2131, CE2407A. Ah! EE2012 and ST2334 ARE mutually exclusive. So I cannot take both. I must choose one for the CS3263 prerequisite branch. If I choose EE2012, I need MA1511+1512. If I choose ST2334, I need MA1505/1511/1512/1521/2002. Let's try ST2334. Sem 1: CS1010, MA1511, MA1512. Sem 2: CS2040C, MA1522, ST2334. Sem 3: CS2109S. Sem 4: CS3263. Sem 5: CS4246. This works. But wait, CS4246 also requires the other branch: (EE2012A or EE2012 or ST2132 or ST2334 or ...). I have ST2334 in Sem 2. So that branch is satisfied. So the plan is valid. Why did the user say it breaks rules? Maybe I missed that CS1231 is not needed. I removed it. The user said "CS1231 was added but no later planned course needs it". In my previous plan, I added CS1231. I should not have. In the new plan, I don't add CS1231. So that rule is satisfied. The user also said "EE2012 and ST2334 exclude each other". In my previous plan, I had both. In the new plan, I only have ST2334 (or only EE2012). If I use ST2334, I don't use EE2012. So that rule is satisfied. So why NO_PLAN? Let's re-read the mutual exclusions. EE2012 mutually exclusive with ST2334. Correct. So I can't take both. I must take one. If I take ST2334, I satisfy the CS3263 stat prereq and the CS4246 stat prereq. If I take EE2012, I satisfy the CS3263 stat prereq and the CS4246 stat prereq. Both are valid paths. So a plan exists. Status should be PLAN.

Let's construct the plan without CS1231 and without EE2012 (using ST2334 instead).
Sem 1: CS1010, MA1511, MA1512, IS1108 (14 MC)
Sem 2: CS2040C, MA1522, ST2334 (12 MC)
